mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 4% signals monetary easing, which may stimulate equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing consumer and business spending.
failure_condition: Forward 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative in >40% of cases when FEDFUNDS < 4%, indicating no positive market response to rate cuts.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects stronger consumer demand and economic expansion, which should positively impact equity markets as higher demand drives corporate revenues.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase by >5% YoY but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative, indicating no transmission of housing demand to broader equity markets.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market weakness, which may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative equity returns as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate rises above 5% but S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in >50% of cases, indicating no negative market response to labor market weakness.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger supply-side activity, which should support equity markets through improved corporate output and profitability.
failure_condition: Industrial production increases by >2% but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative, indicating no positive market response to supply-side growth.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both unemployment (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicate labor market contradictions that may confuse market participants and lead to equity market volatility.
failure_condition: UNRATE and PAYEMS both increase but S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in >60% of cases, indicating no negative market response to conflicting labor signals.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) combined with high unemployment (UNRATE) create a mixed signal about economic health, potentially leading to uncertainty and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 4% and UNRATE > 4% but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in >50% of cases, indicating no negative market response to mixed monetary and labor signals.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real federal funds rate (RSAFS) below $700 billion indicates reduced consumer demand, which may negatively impact equity markets as corporate revenues decline.
failure_condition: RSAFS < $700 billion but S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in >40% of cases, indicating no negative market response to reduced demand.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2% indicates strong economic expansion, which should positively impact equity markets through higher corporate earnings and consumer spending.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth > 2% but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative, indicating no positive market response to economic expansion.
